---
title: "Frequently asked questions"
description: "Answers about surveyframe: using it for a thesis, preregistering on OSF, working without code, collecting answers, and checking a questionnaire file."
---

## Can I use surveyframe for my thesis?

Yes. Start from one of the [studies](../studies.html), replace its questions
with yours, and submit the pre-analysis plan to your supervisor or ethics
committee before you collect data. The report follows APA 7.

## Does it work without coding?

Yes. After `install.packages("surveyframe")`, everything runs in SurveyStudio,
opened from RStudio's Addins menu. See [Get started](../start.html).

## How do I preregister my analysis plan on OSF?

Write the pre-analysis plan from SurveyStudio, or with `render_report()` and
no data, and upload it to OSF or Zenodo with the `.sframe` file. The plan
names the file's hash, so the registration identifies the exact instrument.

## How are answers collected?

SurveyStudio's Collect screen downloads the survey as 1 HTML file, which you
can put on any web host or send. With a Google Sheet and its Apps Script
collector, each answer is stored in a sheet you own. No server is needed.

## How does a reader check that a questionnaire was not changed?

Open the `.sframe` file at [surveyframe.org/verify](https://surveyframe.org/verify/).
A file changed after it was sealed fails the check, and a change made on the
record shows in its amendment log.

## Are the demo data real?

No. The demos' responses are simulated. Each respondent id starts with
`DEMO-`, and every result and report made from them says "demonstration data".

## How do I cite surveyframe?

See [Cite surveyframe](../cite.html).
